nodes.statement:
Let $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ be a reflexive real Banach space with norm $\|\cdot\|$
and let $\pair{\cdot}{\cdot}$ be the duality pairing between
$\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ and its topological dual $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*$.
nodes.name: Duality pairing

nodes.statement:
A set-valued operator 
$M\colon\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\to 2^{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}$ with graph
$\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M=\menge{(x,x^*)\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}\times\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}{x^*\in Mx}$ is monotone if 
\begin{equation}
(\forall (x_1,x_1^*)\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M)(\forall (x_2,x_2^*)\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M)\quad
\pair{x_1-x_2}{x_1^*-x_2^*}\ensuremath{\geqslant} 0,
\end{equation}
and maximally monotone if, furthermore, there exists no monotone 
operator from $\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$ to $2^{\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}^*}$ the graph of which properly 
contains $\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} M$.
nodes.name: Monotone and maximally monotone operator
nodes.statement_short: Monotone operator: nonnegative pairing of graph differences; maximal if its graph has no proper monotone extension.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.1
nodes.statement_short: Write $Z$ as the zero set of the maximally monotone operator $M+S$ (monotone plus skew), then verify each item via monotonicity and graph closedness.

nodes.statement:
Set $\boldsymbol{M}\colon\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}\to
2^{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}^*}\colon(x,y^*)\mapsto 
Ax\times B^{-1}y^*$ and
$\boldsymbol{S}\colon\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}
\to\boldsymbol{\mathcal{X}}^*\colon (x,y^*)\mapsto (L^*y^*,-Lx)$.
Since $A$ and $B^{-1}$ are maximally monotone, so is 
$\boldsymbol{M}$. On the other hand, $\boldsymbol{S}$ is linear, 
bounded, and positive since 
\begin{equation} (\forall(x,y^*)\in\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}})\quad
\pair{\boldsymbol{S}(x,y^*)}{(x,y^*)}=
\pair{x}{L^*y^*}+\pair{-Lx}{y^*}=0. 
\end{equation}
Thus, it follows from \cite[Section~17]{Simo08} that 
$\boldsymbol{S}$ is maximally monotone with 
$\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}\boldsymbol{S}=\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$. In turn, we derive from 
\cite[Theorem~24.1(a)]{Simo08} that
\begin{equation} \boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S}\;\text{is maximally monotone.}
\end{equation}
nodes.name: Monotone+skew reformulation
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $M=A\times B^{-1}$ and skew $S$; show $M+S$ is maximally monotone.

nodes.statement:
\ref{ppOlk28ha12ia}:
Let $(x,y^*)\in\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$. Then
\begin{eqnarray} \boldsymbol{0}\in\boldsymbol{M}(x,y^*)+\boldsymbol{S}(x,y^*)
&\Leftrightarrow& 0\in Ax+L^*y^*\quad\text{and}\quad 0\in 
B^{-1}y^*-Lx\nonumber\\
&\Leftrightarrow& -L^*y^*\in Ax
\quad\text{and}\quad Lx\in B^{-1}y^*\nonumber\\
&\Leftrightarrow& (x,y^*)\in \boldsymbol{Z}.
\end{eqnarray}
Therefore, we derive from \eqref{egVxZ5y820} and
\cite[Lemma~1.1(a)]{IVBro65} that
$\boldsymbol{Z}=\ensuremath{\text{\rm zer}\,}(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})=
(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})^{-1}(0)$ is closed and convex.
nodes.name: Item (i)(a): Z closed convex
nodes.statement_short: $Z=\mathrm{zer}(M+S)$, hence closed and convex.

nodes.statement:
\ref{ppOlk28ha12ib}: Let $x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$. Then
$x\in\mathscr{P}\Leftrightarrow
0\in Ax+L^*BLx\Leftrightarrow (\ensuremath{\exists\,} y^*\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*)\; 
[-L^*y^*\in Ax\;\text{and}\;y^*\in BLx]
\Leftrightarrow (\ensuremath{\exists\,} y^*\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*)\;(x,y^*)
\in\boldsymbol{Z}$. 
Hence $\mathscr{P}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$
$\Leftrightarrow$ $\boldsymbol{Z}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$.
Likewise, let $y^*\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*$. Then 
$y^*\in\mathscr{D}\Leftrightarrow
0\in-LA^{-1}(-L^*y^*)+B^{-1}y^*
\Leftrightarrow(\ensuremath{\exists\,} x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}})\; 
[x\in A^{-1}(-L^*y^*)\;\text{and}\;0\in-Lx+B^{-1}y^*]
\Leftrightarrow(\ensuremath{\exists\,} x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}})\; 
[-L^*y^*\in Ax\;\text{and}\; Lx\in B^{-1}y^*]
\Leftrightarrow(\ensuremath{\exists\,} x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}})\;(x,y^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$.
nodes.name: Item (i)(b): projections of Z
nodes.statement_short: Characterize primal and dual solutions as projections of $Z$.

nodes.statement:
\ref{ppOlk28ha12ib}: Let $x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}}$. Then
$x\in\mathscr{P}\Leftrightarrow
0\in Ax+L^*BLx\Leftrightarrow (\ensuremath{\exists\,} y^*\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*)\; 
[-L^*y^*\in Ax\;\text{and}\;y^*\in BLx]
\Leftrightarrow (\ensuremath{\exists\,} y^*\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*)\;(x,y^*)
\in\boldsymbol{Z}$. 
Hence $\mathscr{P}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$
$\Leftrightarrow$ $\boldsymbol{Z}\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$.
nodes.name: Primal side
nodes.statement_short: Primal solutions are the $x$-projection of $Z$.

nodes.statement:
Likewise, let $y^*\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal Y}}^*$. Then 
$y^*\in\mathscr{D}\Leftrightarrow
0\in-LA^{-1}(-L^*y^*)+B^{-1}y^*
\Leftrightarrow(\ensuremath{\exists\,} x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}})\; 
[x\in A^{-1}(-L^*y^*)\;\text{and}\;0\in-Lx+B^{-1}y^*]
\Leftrightarrow(\ensuremath{\exists\,} x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}})\; 
[-L^*y^*\in Ax\;\text{and}\; Lx\in B^{-1}y^*]
\Leftrightarrow(\ensuremath{\exists\,} x\in\ensuremath{{\mathcal X}})\;(x,y^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$.
nodes.name: Dual side
nodes.statement_short: Dual solutions are the $y^*$-projection of $Z$.

nodes.name: Item (i)(c)
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from (i)(b).

nodes.statement:
\ref{ppOlk28ha12iia} :
Let $\mathsf{a}\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} A$ and $\mathsf{b}\in\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,} B$. Then
$\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0}$
$\Rightarrow$ 
[$-L^*b^*=a^*\in Aa$ and $La=b\in B^{-1}b^*$] 
$\Rightarrow$ $(a,b^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$. In 
addition, 
\begin{multline}
\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\eta_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\pair{a}{a^*}
+\pair{b}{b^*}=\pair{a}{-L^*b^*}+\pair{La}{b^*}\\
=-\pair{La}{b^*}+\pair{La}{b^*}=0.
\end{multline}
Thus 
$\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0}$
$\Rightarrow$ $\boldsymbol{H}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$. 
Conversely, 
$\boldsymbol{H}_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}$ $\Rightarrow$ 
$\boldsymbol{s}^*_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=\boldsymbol{0}$
$\Rightarrow$ $\eta_{\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b}}=0$.
nodes.name: Item (ii)(a): degenerate half-spaces
nodes.statement_short: If $s^*_{a,b}=0$ then $(a,b^*)\in Z$, $\eta_{a,b}=0$ and $H_{a,b}$ is the whole space.

nodes.name: Item (ii)(b): Z as intersection of half-spaces
nodes.statement_short: Show both inclusions between $Z$ and $\bigcap H_{a,b}$.

nodes.name: Intersection inside Z
nodes.statement_short: Maximality of $M$ gives $\bigcap H_{a,b}\subset Z$.

nodes.name: Z inside each half-space
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of $A,B$ gives $Z\subset H_{a,b}$.

nodes.statement:
\ref{ppOlk28ha12iii}: 
Set $(\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})$ $\boldsymbol{x}_n=(a_n,b_n^*)$ and 
$\boldsymbol{x}_n^*=(a_n^*+L^*b_n^*,b_n-La_n)$. Then 
$\boldsymbol{x}_n\ensuremath{\:\rightharpoonup\:} (x,y^*)$, 
$\boldsymbol{x}_n^*\to \boldsymbol{0}$, and $(\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})$ 
$(\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_n^*)\in
\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,}(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})$. 
However, it follows from \eqref{egVxZ5y820} that 
$\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,}(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})$ is sequentially closed 
in $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}^{\text{weak}}\times\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mathcal X}}^{*\text{strong}}$ 
\cite[Lemma~1.2]{IVBro65}. Hence, 
$\boldsymbol{0}\in(\boldsymbol{M}+\boldsymbol{S})(x,y^*)$, 
i.e., by \eqref{egVxZ5y828}, $(x,y^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}$.
nodes.name: Item (iii): weak-strong closedness
nodes.statement_short: Graph of the maximally monotone $M+S$ is weak-strong sequentially closed.

nodes.statement: Consider the setting of Problem~\ref{prob:1}. Then the following hold: \begin{enumerate} \item $\boldsymbol{f}$ is a Legendre function. \item The solution $(\overline{x},\overline{y}^*)$ to Problem~\ref{prob:1} exists and is unique. \end{enumerate}

assumptions: the setting of Problem~\ref{prob:1}
conclusions: The solution $(\overline{x},\overline{y}^*)$ to Problem~\ref{prob:1} exists and is unique.
nodes.label: pvb8uh4504

strictly monotone \cite[Theorem~2.4.4(ii)]{IVZali02} and 
$\nabla h+\gamma A$ is likewise. Let $(x^*,x_1)$ and 
$(x^*,x_2)$ be two elements in $\ensuremath{\text{\rm gra}\,}(\nabla h+\gamma A)^{-1}$

$\nabla h+\gamma A$ implies that 
\begin{equation}

\end{equation}
which is impossible. Thus,
\begin{equation} (\nabla h+\gamma A)^{-1}\;\text{is at most single-valued}.
\end{equation} 
The same argument shows that
\begin{equation} (\nabla j+\mu B)^{-1}\;\text{is at most single-valued}.
\end{equation}

$(x,y^*)\in\boldsymbol{Z}\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}$.

\end{cases}
\end{equation}

$\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} B\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} j\neq\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}$. It therefore follows from
Lemma~\ref{IVlhHg7yG02} that
\begin{equation} \nabla h+\gamma A=(\nabla h+\varepsilon A)+(\gamma-\varepsilon)A 
\quad\text{and}\quad
\nabla j+\mu B=(\nabla j+\delta B)+(\mu-\delta)B
\;\;\text{are coercive}.
\end{equation}

\eqref{4e:single3}, and Proposition~\ref{IVpp:20a} assert 
that the operators
\begin{equation} \begin{cases}

\begin{equation} (\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})\quad

\end{equation}

Proposition~\ref{ppOlk28ha12}\ref{ppOlk28ha12iib},
\eqref{IVe:Bfg+uh4f9-09h}, and 
Definition~\ref{d:B-haugazeau} that
\begin{equation} (\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})\quad
\ensuremath{{\varnothing}}\neq\boldsymbol{C}\subset\boldsymbol{Z}\subset\boldsymbol{H}_n
=H^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}).

\eqref{e:2001}, we see that
\begin{equation} (\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})\quad
P_{\boldsymbol{H}_n}^{\boldsymbol{f}}
\colon\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}\to
\boldsymbol{H}_n\cap\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}

sequences in $\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} f$ and $\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} g^*$, respectively.

\ref{IVt:1ia}$\Rightarrow$\ref{IVt:1ib}: Clear.

\ref{IVt:1ib}$\Rightarrow$\ref{IVt:1ic}: Clear by

\ref{IVt:1ic}$\Rightarrow$\ref{IVt:1id}: In view of 
\eqref{IVe:Bfg+uh4f9-09h},
\begin{align}
0
&\ensuremath{\geqslant}\pair{x_n}{a_n^*+L^*b_n^*}
+\pair{b_n-La_n}{y_n^*}-\pair{a_n}{a_n^*}-\pair{b_n}{b_n^*}
\nonumber\\
&=\pair{x_n-a_n}{a_n^*+L^*y_n^*}+\pair{Lx_n-b_n}{b_n^*-y_n^*}
\nonumber\\
&=\gamma_n^{-1}\pair{x_n-a_n}{\nabla h(x_n)-\nabla h(a_n)}
+\mu_n^{-1}\pair{Lx_n-b_n}{\nabla j(Lx_n)-\nabla j(b_n)}.
\end{align}
Consequently, the strict monotonicity of $\nabla h$ and $\nabla j$ 
yields
\begin{equation}
x_n=a_n\quad\text{and}\quad Lx_n=b_n.
\end{equation}
Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
b_n^*=\mu_n^{-1}\big(\nabla j(Lx_n)-\nabla j(b_n)\big)+y_n^*
=\mu_n^{-1}\big(\nabla j(b_n)-\nabla j(b_n)\big)+y_n^*
=y_n^*.
\end{equation}

\ref{IVt:1id}$\Rightarrow$\ref{IVt:1ie}: We derive from 
\eqref{IVe:Bfg+uh4f9-09h} that
$a_n^*=\gamma_n^{-1}(\nabla h(x_n)-\nabla h(a_n))-L^*y_n^*
=-L^*y_n^*=-L^*b_n^*$. On the other hand, since
\begin{align} \pair{La_n-b_n}{\nabla j(La_n)-\nabla j(b_n)}
&=\pair{Lx_n-b_n}{\nabla j(Lx_n)-\nabla j(b_n)}\nonumber\\
&=\mu_n\pair{Lx_n-b_n}{b_n^*-y_n^*}\nonumber\\
&=0,
\end{align}
the strict monotonicity of $\nabla j$ yields $La_n=b_n$.

\ref{IVt:1ie}$\Leftrightarrow$\ref{IVt:1if}: 
Proposition~\ref{ppOlk28ha12}\ref{ppOlk28ha12iia}.

\ref{IVt:1if}$\Rightarrow$\ref{IVt:1ig}: Indeed,
$\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}=P_{\boldsymbol{H}_n}^{\boldsymbol{f}}
\boldsymbol{x}_n=\boldsymbol{x}_n$.

\ref{IVt:1ig}$\Rightarrow$\ref{IVt:1ih}: We have
\begin{equation} \boldsymbol{x}_{n+1}=Q^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_0,
\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2})=
P^{\boldsymbol{f}}_{H^{\boldsymbol{f}}
(\boldsymbol{x}_0,\boldsymbol{x}_n)\cap H^{\boldsymbol{f}}
(\boldsymbol{x}_n,\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2})}
\boldsymbol{x}_0=P^{\boldsymbol{f}}_{H^{\boldsymbol{f}}
(\boldsymbol{x}_0,\boldsymbol{x}_n)}\boldsymbol{x}_0
=\boldsymbol{x}_n.
\end{equation}

\ref{IVt:1ih}$\Rightarrow$\ref{IVt:1ig}:  By
Proposition~\ref{p:2}\ref{p:2iii-},
$0\ensuremath{\leqslant} D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2},\boldsymbol{x}_n)
\ensuremath{\leqslant} D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1},\boldsymbol{x}_n)=0$.
Therefore 
$D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2},\boldsymbol{x}_n)=0$
and we derive from \cite[Lemma~7.3(vi)]{Ccm01}
that $\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}=\boldsymbol{x}_n$.

\ref{IVt:1ig}$\Rightarrow$\ref{IVt:1ic}: Indeed,
$\boldsymbol{x}_n=\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}=
P^{\boldsymbol{f}}_{\boldsymbol{H}_n}
\boldsymbol{x}_n\in\boldsymbol{H}_n$.

\ref{IVt:1id}$\Rightarrow$\ref{IVt:1ib}: 
We derive from \eqref{IVe:Bfg+uh4f9-09h} that
\begin{equation} \nabla h(x_n)-\gamma_n L^*y_n^*\in\nabla h(a_n)+\gamma_n Aa_n
=\nabla h(x_n)+\gamma_n Ax_n. 
\end{equation}
Hence $-L^*y_n^*\in Ax_n$. Likewise, as in 
\eqref{IWeQA8h33-30a}, we first obtain $Lx_n=b_n$ and then
\begin{equation} \nabla j(Lx_n)+\mu_n y_n^*\in\nabla j(b_n)+\mu_n Bb_n
=\nabla j(Lx_n)+\mu_n B(Lx_n).
\end{equation}
Thus, $y_n^*\in B(Lx_n)$, i.e., $Lx_n\in B^{-1}y_n^*$.
In view of \eqref{IVe:VKT}, the implication is proved.

\ref{IVt:1iv}: 
Proposition~\ref{p:2}\ref{p:2i} implies that
$(\boldsymbol{x}_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}$ is a bounded sequence 
in $\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,}\boldsymbol{f}$. In turn, 
\begin{equation} (x_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\in(\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} f)^{\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\quad\text{and}\quad
(y^*_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\in(\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} g^*)^{\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\quad\text{are bounded}.
\end{equation}
On the other hand, by \eqref{IVe:Bfg+uh4f9-09h},
\begin{equation} (\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})\quad
(x_{n+1/2},y_{n+1/2}^*)=
\boldsymbol{x}_{n+1/2}=P_{\boldsymbol{H_n}}^{\boldsymbol{f}}
\boldsymbol{x}_n\in\boldsymbol{H}_n
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} (\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})\quad\pair{x_{n+1/2}}{a_n^*+L^*b_n^*}
+\pair{b_n-La_n}{y_{n+1/2}^*}
=\pair{a_n}{a_n^*}+\pair{b_n}{b_n^*}.
\end{equation}
Therefore,
\begin{align} (\forall n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N})\quad
&\|x_n-x_{n+1/2}\|\,\|a_n^*+L^*b_n^*\|
+\|b_n-La_n\|\,\|y_n^*-y_{n+1/2}^*\|\nonumber\\
&\ensuremath{\geqslant}\pair{x_n-x_{n+1/2}}{a_n^*+L^*b_n^*}
+\pair{b_n-La_n}{y_n^*-y_{n+1/2}^*}\nonumber\\
&=\pair{x_n}{a_n^*+L^*b_n^*}
+\pair{b_n-La_n}{y_n^*}
-\pair{a_n}{a_n^*}-\pair{b_n}{b_n^*}\nonumber\\
&=\pair{x_n-a_n}{a_n^*+L^*y_n^*}
+\pair{Lx_n-b_n}{b_n^*-y_n^*}\nonumber\\
&=\gamma_n^{-1}\pair{x_n-a_n}{\nabla h(x_n)
-\nabla h(a_n)}+\mu_n^{-1}
\pair{Lx_n-b_n}{\nabla j(Lx_n)-\nabla j(b_n)}
\nonumber\\
&\ensuremath{\geqslant}\sigma^{-1}\big(D^h(x_n,a_n)+D^h(a_n,x_n)
+D^j(Lx_n,b_n)+D^j(b_n,Lx_n)\big)\nonumber\\
&\ensuremath{\geqslant}\sigma^{-1}\big(D^h(x_n,a_n)+D^j(Lx_n,b_n)\big).
\end{align}
However, since \ref{IVt:1iii} yields
\begin{equation} D^f(x_{n+1/2},x_n)\to 0
\quad\text{and}\quad
D^{g^*}(y_{n+1/2}^*,y_n^*)\to 0
\end{equation}
and since $f$ and $g^*$ satisfy Condition~\ref{IVC:1}, 
\eqref{IVbcn5y713b} yields
\begin{equation} x_{n+1/2}-x_n\to 0
\quad\text{and}\quad
y_{n+1/2}^*-y_n^*\to 0.
\end{equation}
Since $\nabla h$ is uniformly continuous on every bounded subset of 
$\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} h$, Lemma~\ref{IVlKKnhf74g10} asserts that $\nabla h$ 
is bounded on every bounded subset of $\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} h$ and hence, 
since $\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} f\subset\ensuremath{\text{\rm int}\,}\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,} h$ and $L^*$ is bounded, 
it follows from \eqref{eKKnhf74g15a} that
$\big(\nabla h(x_n)-\gamma_nL^*y_n^*\big)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}$ is bounded. 
We therefore deduce from \eqref{4:e12}, 
\eqref{IVe:Bfg+uh4f9-09h},
and Lemma~\ref{IVlKKnhf74g12} that
\begin{equation} (a_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\in(\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} h)^{\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\;\;\text{is bounded}.
\end{equation}
Similarly, since $\nabla j$ is uniformly continuous on every 
bounded subset 
of $\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} j$ and $L(\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} f)\subset\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} j$, it follows 
from \eqref{eKKnhf74g15a} and Lemma~\ref{IVlKKnhf74g10} 
that $\big(\nabla j(Lx_n)+\mu_ny_n^*\big)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}$ is bounded 
and hence \eqref{4:e12}, \eqref{IVe:Bfg+uh4f9-09h},
and Lemma~\ref{IVlKKnhf74g12} yield
\begin{equation} (b_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\in(\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} j)^{\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\;\;\text{is bounded}.
\end{equation} 
Thus, $(\nabla h(x_n))_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}$, $(\nabla h(a_n))_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}$,
$(\nabla j(Lx_n))_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}$, and $(\nabla j(b_n))_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}$ 
are bounded and we deduce from \eqref{IVe:Bfg+uh4f9-09h} that 
\begin{equation} (a^*_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}\quad\text{and}\quad(b^*_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}
\quad\text{are bounded}.
\end{equation}
We therefore derive from 
\eqref{IVe:8re84}, \eqref{IVe:IV5}, \eqref{4:e18}, and 
\eqref{4:e19} that
\begin{equation} D^h(x_n,a_n)\to 0\quad\text{and}\quad
D^j(Lx_n,b_n)\to 0.
\end{equation}
Since $h$ and $j$ satisfy Condition~\ref{IVC:1}, we get
\begin{equation} x_n-a_n\to 0\quad\text{and}\quad Lx_n-b_n\to 0.
\end{equation}
Therefore, since $\nabla h$ is uniformly continuous on every 
bounded subset of $\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} h$ and $\nabla j$ is uniformly 
continuous on every bounded subset of $\ensuremath{\text{\rm int\,dom}\,} j$,
\begin{equation} \nabla h(x_n)-\nabla h(a_n)\to 0\quad\text{and}\quad
\nabla j(Lx_n)-\nabla j(b_n)\to 0.
\end{equation}
Hence, using \eqref{IVe:Bfg+uh4f9-09h}, we get
\begin{equation} a_n^*+L^*y_n^*\to 0
\quad\text{and}\quad 
b_n^*-y_n^*\to 0.
\end{equation}
Now, let 
$\boldsymbol{x}=(x,y^*)\in\ensuremath{{\mathfrak W}}(\boldsymbol{x}_n)_{n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb N}}$,
say $\boldsymbol{x}_{k_n}\ensuremath{\:\rightharpoonup\:}\boldsymbol{x}$. 
Then $x_{k_n}\ensuremath{\:\rightharpoonup\:} x$ and $y_{k_n}^*\ensuremath{\:\rightharpoonup\:} y^*$, and we 
derive from \eqref{IVe:IV10} and \eqref{IVe:IV13} that
\begin{equation} \begin{cases}
a_{k_n}\ensuremath{\:\rightharpoonup\:} x\\
b^*_{k_n}\ensuremath{\:\rightharpoonup\:} y^*
\end{cases}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\begin{cases}
La_{k_n}-b_{k_n}\to 0\\
a^*_{k_n}+L^*b^*_{k_n}\to 0.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
It therefore follows from \eqref{eKKnhf74g04},
Proposition~\ref{ppOlk28ha12}\ref{ppOlk28ha12iii},
and \eqref{eKKnhf74g15a} that
$\boldsymbol{x}\in\boldsymbol{Z}\cap\overline{\ensuremath{\text{\rm dom}\,}}\boldsymbol{f}
=\boldsymbol{C}$. Hence, we derive from 
Proposition~\ref{p:2}\ref{p:2iv} that 
\begin{equation} D^{f}({x}_n,\overline{x})+D^{g^*}(y^*_n,\overline{y}^*)=
D^{\boldsymbol{f}}(\boldsymbol{x}_n,\overline{\boldsymbol{x}})\to 0,
\end{equation}
where $\overline{\boldsymbol{x}}=(\overline{x},\overline{y}^*)$.
Hence, $D^{f}({x}_n,\overline{x})\to 0$, 
$D^{g^*}(y^*_n,\overline{y}^*)\to 0$, and, 
since $f$ and $g^*$ satisfy Condition~\ref{IVC:1}, we conclude
that $x_n\to\overline{x}$ and $y^*_n\to\overline{y}^*$.
